is_anopheles.evidence: The study is an epidemiological case-control study in human populations assessing the effectiveness of LLINs and IRS against Plasmodium falciparum malaria; it does not collect or study mosquitoes directly.

reports_target_markers.evidence: No primary genotyping was conducted. The paper only mentions kdr frequency in passing in the study area description by citing a project report (page 3: 'The allelic frequency of the kdr mutation was very high in both areas: 95% in Djougou and 100% in Cobly [21]').

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No primary genotype counts, allele counts, or mosquito sample sizes are presented.

african_field_population.evidence: No mosquito field populations were sampled or tested in this study.

is_primary_study.evidence: It is a primary epidemiological case-control study in humans, but contains no primary mosquito resistance data.

sub_country_location.evidence: Djougou (urban area) and Cobly (rural area), Benin (page 3).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The study was conducted between July and September 2014 (page 4).

assessment.summary: This is an epidemiological case-control study in humans evaluating the real-world effectiveness of LLINs and IRS against P. falciparum infection and uncomplicated clinical malaria in Djougou and Cobly, Benin. No mosquitoes were collected or genotyped.
exclusion_reasons: No primary mosquito insecticide-resistance marker genotyping was performed; vector kdr frequencies mentioned in the study site description are cited from external literature.
No extractable mosquito genotype data (no mosquito sample sizes or genotype counts).
Study examines human epidemiological endpoints rather than Anopheles vector populations.
